cohort: 497 patients who delivered after 24 weeks of gestation in seven Reunion Island maternity hospitals during two weeks in 2019, excluding scheduled caesarean sections
finding: There was no significant difference in satisfaction with pain management between women who delivered with or without neuraxial analgesia.
mod_finding: While there was no difference in satisfaction with pain management, women who delivered without neuraxial analgesia were more likely to have done so by choice, often to achieve a natural birth, or due to rapid labor progression.
